questions.q: Besides a direct sharing-rule change, which of these can also independently trigger an automatic sharing recalculation?
options: Changing a report's chart color
Renaming a custom field's label
A change to the role hierarchy, territory hierarchy, team membership, or a record's ownership
Changing a user's time zone setting
questions.explain: Role hierarchy, public groups, sharing rules, territory hierarchy, user roles, team membership, and record ownership changes can all independently trigger sharing recalculation — a broader list than just explicit sharing-rule edits.

questions.q: Why does sharing recalculation become specifically an LDV problem rather than just a general performance concern?
options: Because sharing recalculation is disabled entirely on objects with more than 1 million records
Because the cost of a recalculation scales with how much data exists to recalculate sharing for, so an operation that's fast on a small org can become slow and resource-intensive on an LDV-scale org
Because sharing recalculation only exists on custom objects
Because LDV orgs are not allowed to use role hierarchies
questions.explain: A sharing recalculation that touches a few hundred records on a small org is routine; the same type of change recalculating access across millions of records on an LDV-scale org is where the cost becomes a real operational concern.

questions.q: What does deferred sharing calculation actually let an administrator do?
options: Temporarily suspend automatic sharing recalculation during a batch of structural changes, then resume it once so recalculation runs in bulk for the whole batch instead of after each individual change
Permanently disable sharing recalculation for the org going forward
Skip creating sharing rules entirely by using Apex instead
Automatically convert all public groups into queues
questions.explain: Deferred sharing calculation suspends recalculation during a bounded batch of structural changes and resumes it once afterward, so the cost is paid a single time across the whole batch rather than once per individual change.

questions.q: Why is deferred sharing calculation described as a bounded maintenance tool rather than a permanent setting?
options: Because it automatically turns itself back on after exactly 24 hours with no admin action
Because it only works on orgs with fewer than 1,000 users
Because Salesforce removes the feature automatically after first use
Because while calculation is deferred, the org's actual record access is out of sync with its current configuration, so it needs to be explicitly resumed once the planned batch of changes is complete
questions.explain: Leaving calculation deferred indefinitely would mean record access doesn't actually reflect the org's real configuration, which is why it's meant for a bounded, planned batch of changes followed by an explicit resume, not a standing setting.

questions.q: In the documented sequencing pattern for a large sharing-model change, what should generally happen once the structural setup work (org-wide defaults, groups, sharing rules, role moves) is complete?
options: Sharing calculation should stay deferred indefinitely to save processing cost
All existing sharing rules should be deleted and rebuilt from scratch
Insert/update-triggered automation (triggers, flows on record creation) should be allowed to resume running normally so validation and enrichment behave correctly in production
The org should be converted to public read/write for all objects
questions.explain: Once the sharing setup itself is finished, automation that fires on insert or update should resume running normally, so that validation and data enrichment continue to work as expected once the maintenance window's structural changes are in place.
